newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks cheer handover with record session.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks cheer handover with record session.

text.p: The Hong Kong stock market smashed through a series of records on Friday, riding a wave of handover euphoria to all-time highs and showing enough momentum to push even higher ahead of the territory's reversion to China.
"Investors are just pushing up the market up ahead of the handover, preparing for the celebration," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
"The upward momentum is still quite strong so unless there is an unexpected event, the market will try to test higher levels ahead of the handover, maybe 15,500 points."

The Hang Seng Index staged its strongest rally in point terms ever on Friday, surging 647.87 points, or 4.47 percent, to close at an all-time high of 15,154.36. The previous all-time high was 15,020.96, hit on June 3 this year.
Turnover was a record HK$26.60 billion (US$3.4 billion), beating the previous record of HK$26.48 billion registered on June 2 this year.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight of June 30 after 156 years of British colonial rule.
"It's a big celebration event and confidence in Hong Kong is high, proved by the Hong Kong stock market," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities.

Shares in Hang Seng Bank Ltd led the rise as Hong Kong's change in sovereignty in 11 days revived speculation that a mainland company could buy a stake in the bank, the second-largest locally incorporated bank in the territory.
The stock surged above HK$100 for the first time ever, rising HK$12.75 to HK$109.50 after hitting a record high at HK$110.00. Shares in its parent, HSBC Holdings Plc, soared HK$7.00 to HK$233.00.
HSBC told Reuters on Friday that it had no plans to change its shareholding, and Hang Seng Bank said it was not aware of any reason for the surge in its share price.

"I don't strongly believe that the Chinese would take a strategic stake in Hang Seng although I am sure that some form of partnership is a possibility between the Hongkong and Shanghai Group, which is owned by HSBC," Peregrine Securities head of research Keith Wu told Reuters Financial Television.
"I think an ownership in the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank or Hang Seng should not be totally ruled out but I think that speculators have overreacted to the situation," he added.
Property stocks also drove the market higher as investors hoped that Hong Kong's new government would avoid imposing draconian measures to curb rising property prices here.

Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd surged HK$3.50 to HK$78.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd gained HK$5.25 to HK$95.25. But with a government move expected soon after the handover, some analysts said investors may turn cautious on the property sector next week.
"A lot of people are preparing to take profit next week," said Ricky Tam, senior research manager at Delta Asia Securities.
He said the market could carry on rising early next week and then run into profit-taking before a long weekend to mark the handover. The Hong Kong market will be closed on June 30, July 1 and July 2.

"I do not rule out the possibility of a slight pullback in the early part of next week. However, I still believe that in the short to medium term I am reasonably positive about the market and I think that the changeover would be something to celebrate," added Wu.
Friday's rise brought this week's gains to 1,041.81 points, or 7.38 percent. The index has risen 12.66 percent this year.
